## Candidate 1: Feminist Structure Signal

* **Title**: ICP Presents *Laia Abril: On Rape and Institutional Failure* & Online Curatorial Discussion
* **Proposed Section**: Feminist Structure Signal
* **Source URL**: `https://www.icp.org/exhibitions/laia-abril-on-rape-and-institutional-failure`
* **Publication / Event Date**: October 15, 2026 (Exhibition run: Oct 15, 2026 – Jan 11, 2027; Curator Panel: Oct 21, 2026)
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * The International Center of Photography (ICP) in New York opened *Laia Abril: On Rape and Institutional Failure*, the second chapter of Spanish research-based artist Laia Abril's ongoing series *A History of Misogyny*.
  * Curated by Sara Ickow (Associate Director of Exhibitions, ICP) and Marta Gili.
  * The exhibition employs forensic aesthetics, archival materials, video, sound, testimonies, and photographs (such as her project *Ala Kachuu* on bride kidnapping in Kyrgyzstan) to examine how state, legal, and social institutions enable systemic sexual violence and victim-blaming.
  * On October 21, 2026, ICP hosted an online discussion featuring historian Joanna Bourke, curator Marta Gili, and Sara Ickow discussing institutional accountability and trauma history.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly intersects with feminist visual culture, biopolitics, forensic aesthetics, counter-archives, and institutional critique of media power.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **New Signal**. ICP was referenced in background context in issue 2026-10-10; this exhibition and curatorial panel are newly opened and previously unrecorded.

## Candidate 2: Visual Culture Signal

* **Title**: Studio Museum in Harlem Announces 2026–27 Artists in Residence Cohort
* **Proposed Section**: Visual Culture Signal
* **Source URL**: `https://studiomuseum.org/press-release/studio-museum-announces-turiya-adkins-timothy-yanick-hunter-and-clifford-prince-king-2026-27-artists-in-residence`
* **Publication Date**: October 21, 2026
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * The Studio Museum in Harlem officially announced on October 21, 2026 that Turiya Adkins, Timothy Yanick Hunter, and Clifford Prince King have been selected for the 2026–27 cohort of its Artist-in-Residence program.
  * The 11-month residency runs from November 2026 through October 2027 inside the museum's newly constructed building (J. Bruce Llewellyn Artist in Residence Center) in Harlem, providing studio space, research support, institutional guidance, a stipend, and a culminating museum exhibition with a publication.
  * The selected artists' practices encompass photography, sound, sculpture, and media art, focusing on Black worldmaking, queer portraiture, and diasporic memory.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Highlights institutional infrastructure, artistic labor, photography, queer portraiture, and diasporic visual archives.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **New Signal**. First entry for this institution and artist cohort.

## Candidate 3: China / East Asia Signal

* **Title**: China Academy of Art Museum Opens Major Retrospective *The Radiance of All Things: A Retrospective of Chu Teh-Chun*
* **Proposed Section**: China / East Asia Signal
* **Source URL**: `https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/21/WS67160ba7a310f1265a1c8c5a.html`
* **Publication / Opening Date**: October 21, 2026
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * The China Academy of Art Museum in Hangzhou opened *The Radiance of All Things: A Retrospective of Chu Teh-Chun* on October 21, 2026 (running until February 18, 2027).
  * The exhibition gathers 107 oil paintings alongside rare drawings, manuscripts, historical photographs, and archival documents tracking the 70-year career of Chu Teh-Chun (1920–2014).
  * It traces his artistic path from his studies in Hangzhou alongside Zao Wou-ki to his relocation to France in 1955, presenting primary photographic and textual records of mid-20th-century East Asian abstraction and transnational artistic exchange.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Provides primary archival, photographic, and historical documents regarding East Asian modernism, transnational artistic migration, and media history.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **New Signal**.

## Candidate 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

* **Title**: Railtown AI Open-Sources Railtracks Swift Agent Development Kit (ADK) on GitHub
* **Proposed Section**: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
* **Source URL**: `https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/227415/Railtown-AI-opensources-Swift-agent-framework-on-GitHub`
* **Publication Date**: October 21, 2026
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * Railtown AI Technologies announced on October 21, 2026 the open-source release of its Railtracks Swift Agent Development Kit (ADK) under the MIT license on GitHub.
  * Expanding on their Python framework, the Swift ADK brings native AI agent orchestration to Apple's macOS/iOS development ecosystem.
  * It allows developers to build agentic workflows that integrate on-device Apple Intelligence local models alongside multi-provider cloud LLMs (including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini).
* **Relevance to Muki**: Materially impacts local, on-device creative technology and knowledge management workflows by providing a native Swift framework for agentic automation on Apple hardware without forcing exclusive cloud API dependency.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **New Signal**.

## Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

* **Title**: The Feminist Institute Digital Archive Launches Michelle Handelman Capsule Collection and Panel at Leslie-Lohman Museum
* **Proposed Section**: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
* **Source URL**: `https://www.thefeministinstitute.org/events/michelle-handelman-capsule-collection-launch`
* **Event Date**: October 28, 2026 (Announcement and registration opened late October 2026)
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * The Feminist Institute (TFI) has launched artist Michelle Handelman's capsule collection within its open digital archive platform.
  * To activate the collection, TFI and Leslie-Lohman Museum of Art (NYC) are co-presenting an in-person panel discussion, *Activating the Archive*, on October 28, 2026.
  * Panelists include Michelle Handelman, Dr. Amber Musser, Jeanne Vaccaro, and Exx Nottage, moderated by Stamatina Gregory.
  * The event focuses on digital information activism, how queer and feminist digital archives intervene in dominant institutional art historical canons, and methods for reclaiming historically marginalized visual histories.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Directly addresses digital archiving, counter-canons, feminist media archaeology, and information activism for marginalized visual histories.
* **Duplication Assessment**: **New Signal**.
